correctness.rationale: Every simple cycle of a block is the union of two terminal paths; edge negative-cycle rank is the number of opposite-sign paths. Any maximum-rank edge on a negative cycle lies on a minority path, or on either side of an exact tie. A flip always lowers the sum of minority counts by exactly one. The same sum is the minimum possible number of sign reversals by the blockwise path-parity lower bound, so convergence is all-choice and shortest. The negative-cycle energy decrement is r-2d+1. Conditional uniform pair and edge selection yields the exact rational length-biased tie formula. The standalone exhaustive checker reproduced 9168 signing cases, 77792 admissible transitions and exact tie checks.

value.rationale: A literature-motivated noncomplete network class with unbounded overlapping cycles admits deterministic, every-choice convergence and globally shortest conflict resolution despite known sparse-network blinker risks. The exact rank and path-length tie probability show how local pathway structures influence final group polarity. This is not merely a numeric finite example or a retelling of the known scalar frustration index.
